Members also discussed the old primary school, cemetery projects, 400 Howard Street and 62 Elm Street.

what_happened.line: The Historical Commission heard a proposed minimum maintenance bylaw covering all buildings, supported it in principle, and sent it for research.
A member was assigned to list other communities with such bylaws, contact their officials and consult the building inspector.
The vote on amendments to the demolition delay bylaw was put off to the next meeting at a member's request.
The proposed maintenance bylaw sets a fine per violation, with each day counted as a separate violation.
Members also discussed cemetery projects, including a tree-cutting quote to be paid from donations, and a site visit to 400 Howard Street.

why_it_matters: A minimum maintenance bylaw would put upkeep rules and daily fines on owners of all buildings, and a demolition delay change affects how long a historic building can be held before it is torn down; either would go to a vote later.
The cemetery work named in the minutes is to be paid from donations, not a stated town appropriation.
